summary:
Imagine preparing for a mission to the Moon or Mars using a place on Earth, only to discover that the experiment you rehearsed does not work in the actual planetary environment. This is the gap we set out to address with ANALOG-X.

The platform connects ten terrestrial study and reference environments, including four in Pakistan, with lunar terrain around Shackleton Rim and Martian terrain around Nili Patera. It combines NASA climate and planetary datasets, Earth observation imagery, elevation models, interactive maps, 3D terrain visualizations and evidence-based experiment planning.

Researchers can explore candidate sites, compare environmental and terrain characteristics, investigate 41 experiment pathways across nine research tracks, examine data provenance and limitations, and generate downloadable experiment briefs. Its offline Mission Director and Field Evidence workflows support research planning beyond simple visual similarity.

At its core, the original Analog Transferability & Failure Analysis (ATFA) framework evaluates which experiments can meaningfully be rehearsed at a terrestrial site, where planetary differences limit transfer, and what additional evidence is needed.

By bringing under-characterized Pakistani environments into planetary analog research, ANALOG-X aims to make mission preparation more accessible, transparent and scientifically defensible.
details:
ANALOG-X: Planetary Analog Intelligence & Mission Rehearsal Platform

1. Project Overview

ANALOG-X is an integrated planetary analog research, environmental intelligence and mission-rehearsal platform designed to help researchers investigate where and how terrestrial environments can support preparations for lunar and Martian exploration.

Identifying a terrestrial landscape that resembles the Moon or Mars is not sufficient. Researchers also need to understand which experiments can be performed there, which environmental conditions are relevant, what cannot be replicated, and what evidence is still missing.

ANALOG-X brings these research activities together in one interactive platform, connecting Earth observation, planetary terrain data, environmental analysis, experiment planning, evidence traceability and field-research workflows.

2. Global and Pakistani Analog Discovery

The platform incorporates ten Earth study and reference environments:

Pakistan candidates

  • Chagai small salt playas near Nok Kundi
  • Hamun-i-Mashkel
  • Koh-i-Sultan volcanic field
  • Hispar Glacier

International reference environments

  • Dallol and the Danakil Depression
  • Atacama Desert
  • McMurdo Dry Valleys
  • Haughton impact structure
  • Icelandic volcanic fields
  • Death Valley

These environments are explored in relation to two planetary reference regions: Shackleton Rim near the lunar south pole and Nili Patera on Mars.

The Pakistani locations are under-characterized research candidates, not asserted discoveries or scientifically confirmed planetary equivalents. Their inclusion creates opportunities for further field characterization and expands the geographic diversity of planetary analog research.

3. Earth Observation and Planetary Data Integration

ANALOG-X integrates multiple sources of scientific information:

  • NASA POWER climate profiles for environmental context.
  • NASA Earthdata Common Metadata Repository for scientific dataset discovery.
  • MODIS browse imagery for visual environmental investigation.
  • NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter LOLA elevation products.
  • NASA Mars Global Surveyor MOLA elevation products.
  • NASA Planetary Data System catalogue records.
  • NASA GIBS imagery services.
  • ESA Copernicus Sentinel-2 observations.
  • Copernicus DEM GLO-30 elevation data.

The platform includes processed terrain grids for the ten Earth environments, a lunar terrain grid and a Martian terrain grid. It also provides environmental profiles, imagery exploration and dataset provenance.

These sources are not treated as interchangeable measurements. The platform distinguishes between processed elevation data, gridded climate context, catalogue metadata and browse imagery.

4. Interactive Planetary Research Environment

The application provides an interactive Earth candidate atlas, planetary target selection, location exploration, evidence dashboards, imagery galleries and terrain visualization.

Researchers can:

  • Explore terrestrial candidate environments geographically.
  • Filter and investigate candidates against planetary targets.
  • Compare lunar, Martian and terrestrial terrain context.
  • Explore interactive 3D elevation surfaces.
  • Examine climate and environmental profiles.
  • Investigate the provenance and coverage of supporting datasets.
  • Review experiment pathways and their limitations.
  • Generate downloadable experiment briefs.

The 3D terrain visualizations use local median-relative elevation for comparative exploration. They are not vertically co-registered planetary digital twins and must not be interpreted as landing-safety or rover-trafficability assessments.

5. Experiment Planning and Mission Rehearsal

ANALOG-X organizes 41 experiment pathways across nine research tracks.

Instead of treating an entire landscape as one universal analog, researchers can investigate specific experimental activities and identify which terrestrial environments may support their preparation.

The Analog Transferability & Failure Analysis (ATFA) framework is a central scientific contribution. It records:

  • What can be rehearsed at a particular terrestrial location.
  • Why that location may be relevant.
  • Which planetary differences limit the transfer.
  • Potential failure conditions and invalid assumptions.
  • What additional measurements or field observations are needed.
  • Which data sources support the assessment.

These are transparent, qualitative research-triage assessments, not probabilistic predictions or NASA-certified classifications.

6. Mission Director and Field Evidence Workflows

The platform includes an offline deterministic Mission Director and evidence-review workflow, allowing researchers to work with bundled scientific records without making every operation dependent on an external AI service.

A Field Evidence Passport workflow supports the organization of field observations and evidence. Experiment briefs can be downloaded as structured JSON for further analysis and research planning.

The project also includes a self-hostable FastAPI backend architecture with SQLite support and PostgreSQL compatibility. Optional AI-assisted infrastructure can extend the platform, but the core research and offline workflows are not dependent on a hosted language-model API.

7. Technology and Engineering

The application combines HTML, CSS and JavaScript with Leaflet for interactive mapping and OpenStreetMap for its default basemap.

Its scientific data-processing and discovery workflows use Python. NASA POWER and NASA GIBS provide external data services, while locally bundled research records and processed terrain grids support offline exploration.

The optional backend uses FastAPI, with SQLite for local development and PostgreSQL support for shared deployments.

The project is designed to make its research outputs, source provenance, assumptions and limitations inspectable rather than hiding them behind a single black-box similarity score.

8. Creativity, Innovation and Intended Impact

ANALOG-X brings together planetary analog discovery, geospatial intelligence, Earth observation, terrain exploration, experiment planning and evidence management in a unified research environment.

Its key innovation is moving beyond visual landscape resemblance toward experiment-level transferability and failure analysis.

Its second important contribution is bringing Pakistan's diverse and under-characterized environments into a global planetary analog research workflow.

The platform aims to help researchers plan more meaningful terrestrial experiments, identify evidence gaps before field campaigns, improve transparency in analog selection and support more informed preparation for future lunar and Martian exploration.

9. Scientific Integrity and Limitations

ANALOG-X is a research and planning platform, not a NASA-certified system, landing-site selector, resource certification tool or rover-safety model.

NASA POWER provides gridded climate context rather than local station measurements. MODIS browse JPEGs are not calibrated land-surface-temperature arrays. Sentinel-2 imagery does not independently establish mineralogical composition. Copernicus DEM GLO-30 is a digital surface model, not a bare-earth survey.

The lunar terrain analysis does not establish permanently shadowed-region conditions, water-ice presence or landing safety. The Martian terrain analysis does not establish surface strength or trafficability. Some planetary resource datasets have been discovered and accessed at the catalogue or metadata level but have not been fully ingested and scientifically processed.

The Pakistan candidate environments require additional field validation. All qualitative assessments are presented with their evidence limitations and the additional measurements needed to strengthen them.
